evidence.C1: Test log shows 1 of 10 scripted runs ended in arrest during the first job ('hit a pedestrian... arrested'), risking failure for a stranger.
evidence.C2: Screenshots show visible aliasing (jagged edges) on vehicle and building silhouettes despite 'Pretty' graphics setting.
evidence.C3: Systems interlock deeply: 'no cab pickup, tune-up or wheel ride while wanted' and perks tie side activities together.
evidence.C4: HUD is minimal ('cash and health only'); stars and weapon info hide automatically when not needed.
evidence.C5: Fact sheet plainly states limits: 'No real players have tried it yet' and 'Only tested in Chrome on one Windows laptop'.

fixes: Suppress police wanted levels and arrests during the first job (not just vehicle wrecking) to guarantee 100% tutorial completion.
Enable a post-processing anti-aliasing pass (FXAA or SMAA) in the 'Pretty' graphics preset to smooth jagged model edges.
Display 'Handbrake' and 'Sprint' keys in the visible section of the Title Screen controls by default, rather than folding them away.

evidence.C1: Title screen shows six keys clearly with 'How to Play'; first job cut to under a minute ending at Sol Wheel pier; learner car prevents burning-car frustration; standing-still prompt for walking keys; screenshots show clear progression from title to objective to job completion
evidence.C2: Distinct districts (Meridian towers, Sol Beach pastels, Rustport stencil), 86 painted walls, neon trim, day/night cycle with lit windows; sunset/dusk shots are atmospheric but buildings remain visibly boxy and textures flat in screenshots
evidence.C3: Six story jobs, four odd-job types (Rush Order, Repo Run, Block Dash, Hot Parcel), cab fares with streak bonuses, property with rent, 15 hidden packages, harbor courier, Sol Wheel ride, helicopter at 4 stars, Tune-up shop, perks tying activities together
evidence.C4: HUD reduced to cash and health; stars only when wanted; weapon line only 5s after change; clock moved to map/pause; pause screen is three buttons plus settings and perks; G8 passes no overlaps at three resolutions
evidence.C5: Own names throughout (Meridian, Sol Beach, Rustport, Sol Wheel, Coastliner, Tidal, Vanta GT); explicit 'not affiliated' line; limits stated plainly: 'Only tested in Chrome on one Windows laptop; no phone or gamepad controls' and 'No real players have tried it yet'

fixes: Get real players to test driving feel and jobs beyond the first one — currently only one of six story jobs is driven by real key presses, and the fact sheet admits 'No real players have tried it yet'

Add more architectural detail and silhouette variety to buildings — the boxy, flat-shaded structures visible in most screenshots limit the 'recognisable from one screenshot' atmosphere the rubric's 10-anchor demands
Evaluate and improve the synth radio audio — the fact sheet explicitly lists 'how the synth radio sounds' as not covered by tests, and audio is a major part of atmosphere for a driving game

evidence.C1: First prompt 'Get into the red car ahead [F]' with 'JOB 111 m', then 'Follow the beach road to the Sol Wheel pier'; key-press runs '9 of 10 finished, all nine in 38.6 to 47.3 s' - but 'the tenth hit a pedestrian 25 m short... (BUSTED)', so a stranger's first minute can still end in an arrest before the first job is finished.
evidence.C2: Consistent pastel-neon style across shots: pink-dusk Sol Wheel, teal sea and pastel hotels by day, lit windows and lamp pools at night; but Rustport's flat grey ground and plain night roads stay generic, and the player model is a bare box figure.
evidence.C3: Six story jobs, four odd-job kinds, cab fares, courier shift, property, 15 packages, perks, tune-up and police heat that gates side activities - yet most activities are drive-to-marker variants, odd jobs are 'taken in turn' not chosen, and 'their difficulty and their time limits are not measured'.
evidence.C4: 'The HUD is cash and health'; G8 'no overlaps at 3 sizes'; driving shots show objective, distance, route arrows and minimap reading at a glance; only nit is transient text stacking (perk card plus two message boxes during the wheel ride).
evidence.C5: 'Own city, names and art', G9 'own names only', plus a candid 'Not covered by the tests' section admitting one laptop, no real players and AI judges; only reserve is that the design still mirrors the compared series' structure (stars, respray, BUSTED, hidden packages).

fixes: Make the learner phase arrest-proof: until the first job is done, suppress wanted stars from collisions/pedestrian hits or stop patrol cars from arresting, so 10 of 10 first runs end with the job finished instead of the documented 1-in-10 BUSTED.
Have a human play every job, cab fare and courier shift to tune timers, rewards and difficulty - the fact sheet admits these are only script-passed with the car moved between markers.
Widen activity variety beyond drive-to-marker: let players choose odd-job types instead of a fixed rotation and add on-foot or combat-flavoured tasks so ten minutes feel more varied.
